version_scope: v1 pull subscription concepts; no client or API request executed

primary_sources.verified_point: Default at-least-once delivery and no guaranteed order; deadline expiry can permit redelivery, and a duplicate can occur even after a successful ACK.
primary_sources.packet_use: Motivates idempotent business processing and explicit post-ACK duplicate fixture. No exact timing guarantee is inferred.

primary_sources.verified_point: Exactly-once delivery is pull/regional/message-ID scoped; retry of a published message retains its message ID. This does not merge distinct publications of one business event.
primary_sources.packet_use: Clarifies message identity versus business identity; exactly-once is discussed as a limitation and never enabled.

primary_sources.verified_point: Acknowledge takes delivery ackIds returned by pull; an expired acknowledgment does not safely imply permanent removal under ordinary delivery.
primary_sources.packet_use: Illustrative a-m*-* ACK IDs are distinct from message IDs and business event IDs.

fictional_model_assumptions: Oldest-pending deterministic delivery order and one delivery in flight
Manual simulated expiry and retry with no actual timer or automatic concurrency
Injected first-attempt sink failure for m1 and commit-before-late-ACK crash for m2
Local ledger write and dedup registration are atomic
Modeled ACK attempts succeed; no Google transport-error or RPC validation emulation
Illustrative ack IDs and forced post-ACK duplicate fixture
Fixed additive cent events, no refunds, currency conversion, updates or actual cloud sink
